findings.title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and moves
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing groups to the top level. Consequently, an administrator granted only read access to all groups can perform these mutations. This check must require MANAGE, with a regression test verifying that VIEW alone cannot create or move groups.

findings.title: Use group model IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: Authorization resources for individual groups are named with the group model ID, but have their own separately generated resource ID. This loop passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), which looks up a resource by name, so it fails to evaluate the individual group's permission and instead falls back to all-groups permissions. It also returns authorization resource IDs as group IDs, which UsersResource passes to the user storage membership filter and count queries. Thus individual view-members/manage-members grants do not reliably populate user searches or counts. Evaluate the resource using its group-model name and return actual group model IDs; the synthetic all-groups resource must also be handled separately rather than returned as a group ID.

findings.title: Group membership filtering excludes users with direct user permissions
findings.body: When an administrator lacks global user-view permission, any nonempty result from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() becomes a mandatory storage-level group membership filter. V2 also supports direct permissions on individual users, so an administrator allowed to view Alice directly and members of Bob's group should see both Alice and Bob. This query excludes Alice before usersEvaluator.canView() can evaluate her direct grant. The candidate search must include the union of directly authorized users and users authorized through groups, rather than restricting all candidates to the permitted groups. The brute-force user search has the same problem.
